title: Estes looks back from the cockpit, Rosethorn 007
description: A helmeted man in the front seat turns in flight to smile back at the camera, visor down and boom mic at his lips, EMERGENCY EXIT stenciled on the yellow cockpit frame beside him; at the left edge the other seat is partly in view. "Just taking off on the flight line heading to Nui Ba Den." Looking again on 2026-09-12, Larry named him Estes. The man looking back was not the one flying: "Usually the guy looking back is not flying the plane and he was talking to me." The pilot, he thinks, was Geutler, "possibly to the left of Estes." Larry remembers marathon days aboard Rosethorn 007 — once taking off at 4 a.m., refueling at Qui Nhơn (where he bought his camera at the PX), and returning at 11 at night, rain clouds pouring down across the country.
researchNotes: Two accounts, in the later of which Larry corrects the earlier: 2026-08-15 (giscus-vn-0016-c18032603.json) and 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0016-c18415741.json and -c18415765.json), 'Location: Ton Son Nhut', taking off for Núi Bà Đen, and the name Estes. HOW THE NAME ARRIVED: his son told him it looked like there was a name on the helmet, and Larry read it off the photograph — so 'Estes' is his reading of the lettering, not a memory recovered unprompted. The earlier machine reading of the same lettering is not independent confirmation of it, and a helmet name settles the lettering, not the wearer. The person link changed on his own first-person correction; how, and the earlier name, are kept in research/photos/held-from-records-2026-09-14.md, not repeated here (interview guide, the Estes question). Captain Guegler is not linked: 'possibly' is Larry's hedge, and the seat at left is too little in frame to show anyone. The 2026-08-15 Rosethorn 007 attribution was not withdrawn and stands. Person record: data/people/estes.json; issue #155.
